names: RH San Francisco, The Gallery at the Historic Bethlehem Steel Building
summary: The 1917 Classical Revival main office of the Union Iron Works at the corner of 20th and Illinois Streets, designed by Frederick H. Meyer, rehabilitated by Orton Development under the Port's 66-year Historic Core master lease and subleased whole to RH (Restoration Hardware) on a 41-year sublease from February 2017; RH San Francisco, with the Palm Court restaurant and a rooftop park, opened May 13, 2022.

milestones.text: Built as the Union Iron Works' new main office building to Frederick H. Meyer's design, reported at a cost of $250,000 and 350 staff
Port Commission endorses the Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (Resolution 10-27), which calls for a National Register district and rehabilitation of the 20th Street buildings

Port Commission awards the 20th Street Historic Buildings opportunity to Orton Development after a 2011 RFP; Exclusive Negotiating Agreement approved April 2012; term sheet endorsed October 2012 (Board of Supervisors December 2012)

Historic Preservation Commission informational hearing on the rehabilitation of the ten 20th Street Historic Buildings (case 2013.1168E): ~270,000 gsf existing plus ~69,000 gsf of new mezzanines, ~334,000 gsf total
Union Iron Works Historic District listed in the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 14000150), giving the project access to federal historic tax credits
Port Commission Resolution 14-33 approves the Lease Disposition and Development Agreement and 66-year Master Lease (L-15814) with Historic Pier 70, LLC (Orton) and adopts CEQA findings
Master lease approved by the Board of Supervisors and fully executed, giving Orton site control; construction commences thereafter (September 2015 per the National Trust)
Permanent financing for the Historic Core project achieved

Port Commission update: six of eight buildings complete, Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, project 100% subleased except two atrium retail spaces; total cost revised from $81.9M to an estimated $127.0M
Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a Governor's Historic Preservation Award

Restoration Hardware reported as the Historic Core's first tenant, subleasing Building 101 from Historic Pier 70 LLC; design architect James Gillam of Backen, Gillam & Kroeger; opening then slated for 2017
RH sublease commences: entire building, 41-year term, PDR showroom and restaurant use
Building 101 still under construction with completion and occupancy anticipated in 2020; additions include a publicly accessible restaurant and rooftop terrace
Rehabilitation and tenant improvements scheduled for completion (Port's 2019 milestone list)
RH San Francisco opens at 590 20th Street: five floors, ~80,000 sq ft of galleries, the Palm Court restaurant, two wine bars and a rooftop park

costs.what: Hard cost of the Building 101 rehabilitation (2018 actual/estimate; $13.1M at 2014 approvals)
Reported construction cost of the building in 1917 (San Francisco Chronicle, January 27, 1917, quoted in the NRHP nomination)

facts.value: Orton Development, Inc. through Historic Pier 70, LLC (66-year master lease L-15814 from the Port of San Francisco)
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects (design architect); Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture (historic architect)

Developer equity up to $14 million plus loans; Port participation rent of 50% of revenues above debt and a 14% equity return; sources in 2018: Port capital $1.8M, Seismic Safety Loan $23.6M, historic tax credit equity $20.4M, private debt and equity $81.2M
Contributing resource to the Union Iron Works Historic District (NRHP, listed April 17, 2014)
Classical Revival; three stories with basement (plus sub-basement), concrete and brick, stucco-clad, L-shaped with a beveled corner entry
140 ft 6 in by 51 ft 10 in by 72 ft high (NRHP); 140 ft by 50 ft, 72 ft in D4D Figure 6.5.4
56,268 (NRHP); 61,311 before and 60,525 after rehabilitation, plus a 9,000 sq ft new restaurant building behind it (Port 2019 Table 1); RH describes ~80,000 sq ft over five floors
RH (Restoration Hardware): RH San Francisco gallery, Palm Court restaurant, wine bars, rooftop park
James Gillam, Backen, Gillam & Kroeger (RH's design architect)
Reinforced concrete shear walls; interior partitions removed for an open floor plan (2013 HPC packet)
Union Iron Works / Bethlehem Steel main office; vacant before rehabilitation, formerly office use and one residential unit
All of Building 101 and the new restaurant north of it are listed by the Port as publicly accessible spaces under Master Lease Exhibit K

open_questions: The exact completion / certificate of occupancy date for Building 101 (the Port's 2019 memo anticipated 2020; RH opened May 2022) was not found.

Whether Buildings 122 and 123, the two outbuildings behind Building 104 that share the master lease, are on this parcel or the Building 104 parcel is not settled by any source; this repo's status.csv groups them with the north-side lot.
No 'now' photograph with a stated license was found; RH's press images are the tenant's copyright and are linked, not hosted.
The HAER survey named in the brief was not located in the Library of Congress catalog (see PR description); the NRHP nomination is used as the historic primary source.
